versions_ahb.change: Update for AMBA 5 AHB Protocol Specification (Confidential)
Confidential to Non-Confidential Release of AHB5

New features and enhancements: Signal width properties; Write strobes (HWSTRB); User signaling update (HxUSER); Signal validity rules; Interface protection using parity (HxxCHK signals). Regularized terminology to Manager and Subordinate (from Master/Slave).

versions_apb.change: Second release for APB v1.0 — adds PREADY, PSLVERR (APB3)
First release for APB v2.0 — adds PPROT and PSTRB (APB4)

deprecated_features.rationale: Regularized to Manager / Subordinate for inclusive language. Issue A/B used Master/Slave.
deprecated_features.supports_through: Backward compatible at signal level; terminology change only.

backward_compat_traps.issue_C: ADDR_WIDTH parameterized 10..64; default 32. Components written for fixed 32 must support the parameterized form.

backward_compat_traps.issue_B_C_with_Extended_Memory_Types_pro: 7-bit HPROT[6:0] adding Lookup / Allocate / Shareable bits.

backward_compat_traps.issue_A: No HNONSEC / HEXCL / HMASTER / HEXOKAY / HWSTRB / HxUSER / HxxCHK signals.
backward_compat_traps.issue_B_C: Above signals added behind interface properties (Secure_Transfers / Exclusive_Transfers / Write_Strobes / User_Request_Width / Parity).
All transfers in a locked sequence must be to the same Subordinate address region (Section 3.3 Note).

backward_compat_traps.APB2: PREADY did NOT exist; every transfer is exactly two cycles.
backward_compat_traps.APB3_APB4: PREADY added; Subordinate can extend ACCESS with wait states.

backward_compat_traps.APB2: PSLVERR did NOT exist; no error mechanism.
backward_compat_traps.APB3_APB4: PSLVERR added; Subordinate can signal transfer failure.

backward_compat_traps.APB4: PSTRB[(PWDATA_WIDTH/8)-1:0] added for sparse-write byte-lane support.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Even in APB3/APB4, peripherals are not required to support PSLVERR. If absent, the bridge input is tied LOW.
AHB-to-APB bridge maps PSLVERR to HRESP[0] = ERROR; integrator must wire this correctly.

fields.version_naming_history_note_ahb: AHB-Lite (single-Manager) first defined in Issue A (2006). Issue B introduced 'AHB5' = AHB-Lite + optional Secure / Exclusive / Extended memory / User / Parity features. Issue C (2021) regularized Master/Slave terminology and added Signal validity rules + Write strobes + Parity-based interface protection. In Issue C, the term 'AHB' refers to both AHB-Lite and AHB5; unless stated, signals are common to both.
fields.version_naming_history_note_apb: APB2 (AMBA 2 APB Spec) defined the original two-phase interface. APB3 (ARM IHI 0024B, 2004) added PREADY + PSLVERR. APB4 (ARM IHI 0024C, 2010) added PPROT + PSTRB. APB Rev E (1998) is obsolete and superseded by APB2/APB3/APB4.
interoperability_summary: AHB-Lite Manager interfaces a wider AHB5 Subordinate by leaving the AHB5-specific signal inputs at safe defaults (HEXCL=0, HNONSEC=0, HWSTRB=all-ones).
APB4 Manager interfaces an APB3 Subordinate by tying off PPROT + PSTRB at the Subordinate input (or the bridge does not generate them).
An AHB5 Subordinate interfaces an AHB-Lite Manager by treating absent optional signals as their defaults.

evidence.quote: 06 June 2006 A First release for v1.0; 25 June 2015 B.a Update for AMBA 5 AHB Protocol Specification (Confidential); 30 October 2015 B.b Confidential to Non-Confidential Release; 15 September 2021 C New features and enhancements: Signal width properties, Write strobes, User signaling update, Signal validity rules, Interface protection using parity. Regularized terminology to be Manager and Subordinate.

Issue A of this specification describes the AHB-Lite interface. Issue B introduced AHB5, which is based on AHB-Lite with some added capabilities. This issue of the document is Issue C and adds the following topics: Signal width properties; Write strobes; User signaling update; Interface protection using parity. In this specification, the term AHB is used to refer to both AHB-Lite and AHB5.
HADDR ADDR_WIDTH is recommended to be between 10 and 64. In the issues A and B of this specification, the address width was fixed at 32.

Issue A of this specification defined a 4-bit HPROT signal. Issue B of this specification adds extended memory types. The name of HPROT[3] is changed between Issue A and Issue B of this specification, but the definition remains the same. In Issue A HPROT[3] was designated Cacheable, in Issue B it is designated Modifiable.
25 September 2003 A First release for v1.0; 17 August 2004 B Second release for v1.0; 13 April 2010 C First release for v2.0.

The APB Specification Rev E, released in 1998, is now obsolete and is superseded by the following three revisions: AMBA 2 APB Specification; AMBA 3 APB Protocol Specification v1.0; AMBA APB Protocol Specification v2.0. AMBA 3 adds: Wait states (PREADY); Error reporting (PSLVERR). AMBA APB v2.0 adds: Transaction protection (PPROT); Sparse data transfer (PSTRB).
APB signal PREADY added (in Issue B). APB signal PSLVERR added (in Issue B). APB signal PPROT added (in Issue C). APB signal PSTRB added (in Issue C).
